title: Cosmetics & Crafting Altar
summary: The crafting altar turns gathered materials into wearable cosmetics: hats, back/body cosmetics, balloons, and an off-hand item. It works the same way on every server, so a cosmetic crafted on Diamond Trophy can be worn in the Hub and vice versa. Recipes cost materials (and sometimes network coins), take real time to finish, and are queued in a small number of craft slots that scale with your rank.
how_it_works:
You interact with the altar in one of two ways: right-click the physical crafting altar (an ItemsAdder piece of furniture) wherever it is placed in the world, which is open to every player, or use the /altar command to open the same menu from anywhere on the map, which is an MVIP-and-up convenience rather than a requirement - the furniture itself never requires a rank.

Opening it shows a scrollable list of recipes, filterable by category (Hat, Body, Balloon, Off Hand, or a catch-all). Clicking a recipe opens its detail screen: a card for the cosmetic itself, a row of tiles for each required material showing how many you have versus how many you need, and a Craft button that is only clickable once every requirement is met. Some recipes also cost a chunk of network coins on top of materials, shown separately from the material tiles.

A few of the best cosmetics (currently the Golden Crown, Jetpack, Angel Wings, and Plush) additionally require a matching Blueprint before they can be crafted at all - a permanent, non-consumable unlock item that drops rarely from Rare Crates. Until you find the blueprint, that recipe shows as a locked silhouette in the list; finding the blueprint unlocks the recipe forever, it is not used up by crafting.

Starting a craft consumes the materials (and coins) immediately and begins a countdown; how long a craft takes depends on the cosmetic's rarity unless the recipe overrides it: roughly 5 minutes for Common, 15 minutes for Uncommon, 1 hour for Rare, 4 hours for Epic, 12 hours for Legendary, and 24 hours for Mythic. The countdown keeps running even while you are offline or playing on a different server, and survives a server restart. A separate "Your Crafts" screen on the altar lists everything currently cooking with a live progress bar, and lets you collect a finished job (which grants the cosmetic) or cancel an unfinished one, which refunds everything it cost. A finished-but-uncollected craft keeps occupying its slot until you actually collect it.

How many crafts you can have running at once depends on your rank: Player gets 1 slot, VIP 2, MVIP 3, Elite 4, and Champion (and staff) 5. The altar always shows the maximum number of slots that exists on the server and greys out/locks the ones above your own rank, so you can see what upgrading would unlock. Getting demoted never cancels a craft already in progress - you simply cannot start a new one until you are back under your slot limit.

There is also a plain "Your Materials" screen on the altar that just lists every gathering material you currently hold, useful for checking what you're stocked up on without doing recipe math yourself.

Once you own a cosmetic, hats, back/body cosmetics, and balloons are all equipped through the Cosmetics menu - reached from the player profile menu's Cosmetics button, or directly with the /cosmetics command - which is a separate, third-party wardrobe-style interface, not part of the altar itself. There is also an in-world wardrobe area you can be teleported to for the same purpose. A hat occupies your actual helmet slot; if you put on a real helmet, your hat cosmetic is automatically taken off and held until the helmet comes off again, so a hat and a real helmet are never both trying to render at once.

The off-hand slot is different: it isn't a CosmeticsCore category at all, it's specific to this network. An equipped off-hand cosmetic is only ever shown while your off-hand is genuinely empty - the moment a real item (like a shield or a totem) would go there, the cosmetic simply is not put back, rather than being visibly "kicked out"; it reappears automatically once the off-hand is empty again.
how_to_access: Right-click the physical crafting altar furniture in the world (open to everyone), or use /altar to open the same menu from anywhere (an MVIP+ convenience). Equip owned cosmetics from the profile menu's Cosmetics button (runs /cosmetics) or via the in-world wardrobe.

guis.title: Crafting Altar
guis.description: The main altar interface: browse recipes, see what a recipe costs, start a craft, and manage running crafts.
guis.how_to_open: Right-click the crafting altar furniture, or run /altar (MVIP+).

slots.action: Opens the countdown/collect screen for your running crafts
Opens a flat grid of every gathering material you own
Click to open that recipe's detail screen; greyed tiles are locked (need a blueprint) or unavailable
Cycles the recipe list between Everything, Hat, Body, Balloon, and Off Hand
Pages through the recipe list when there are more recipes than fit on one screen

guis.notes: The detail screen (opened from a recipe tile) shows the cosmetic, its description and rarity, a tile per required material marked have/need, and a Craft button that explains exactly why you can't craft yet (missing blueprint, short on materials, short on coins, or all craft slots busy) when it isn't available. The Your Crafts screen shows one tile per craft slot: a running job with a progress bar, a finished job ready to collect, a free slot, or a slot locked because your rank hasn't unlocked it yet.

guis.title: Cosmetics (Wardrobe)
guis.description: Where you actually put on and take off cosmetics you've unlocked. This screen belongs to a separate third-party plugin (CosmeticsCore), not to the altar, so its exact internal layout isn't something this document can verify in detail.
guis.how_to_open: Profile menu -> Cosmetics button (runs /cosmetics), or the /cosmetics command directly. A separate in-world wardrobe area also exists that a related command can teleport you into.
guis.notes: Covers Hat, Body, and Balloon categories. The off-hand slot is not part of this menu at all (see how_it_works and open_questions).

open_questions: As of this audit, there does not appear to be any in-game command or menu that lets a player choose or switch which off-hand cosmetic is equipped - the underlying equip/unequip function exists in the code but nothing currently calls it. Off-hand recipes (Bouquet, Lantern, Plush) can still be crafted and owned, but whether/how they can be worn may not be settled yet. This could change at any time.
The exact physical location of the crafting altar furniture in the Hub is not written down anywhere in text form that this research could find (it's placed by hand in the world).
The in-world 'wardrobe' teleport command belongs to the third-party CosmeticsCore plugin, not this network's own code, so its exact name/aliases weren't independently verified from source.
Headphones (a hat obtainable only from Rare Crates, not the altar) has no rarity tier listed in configuration, so no rarity is given for it.
